b.a: MII CM PRO Trigger Event Type to NHS Wales PROMs Trigger Event Type

tr.td: Registration for future collections; no content measurement yet.
Collection in primary care before referral to specialised care.
After acceptance of a referral to specialised or inpatient care.
On the occasion of a booked outpatient appointment.
First measurement of a measurement series: admission, enrolment, start of the survey.
Before a planned intervention, e.g. as part of pre-operative assessment.
After a confirmed intervention, usually at a defined interval.
~15 (Wales 15 applies only after the intervention has been confirmed as performed.)
At discharge from inpatient or day-patient treatment.
Scheduled follow-up at a defined interval to a reference event after the end of the treatment episode.
?15 (Wales derives follow-up time points from trigger event plus trigger event date (e.g. 15 Intervention + 6 months); follow-up after discharge would correspond to 16.)
Requested by a treating professional outside a scheduled time point.
Triggered by the patient, e.g. when symptoms worsen.
Routine collection in a non-preselected population to identify conspicuous cases, e.g. PHQ-9 depression screening of all patients at admission.
Occasion-related assessment on suspicion or symptoms, as part of diagnostic classification or severity grading before a treatment decision.
Repeated collection during ongoing treatment for steering or observation, e.g. symptom monitoring during chemotherapy. Unlike follow-up, monitoring takes place within the treatment episode.
Collection to determine a primary, secondary or further endpoint defined in a study protocol; the protocol position names the endpoint.
None of the triggers in this list applies.
